title.en: Hero detail ladder: how much detail at which distance

en: how much detail on a hero object

summary: Authored starting numbers for the three detail bands of a hero object: how many features per square metre of visible surface, how large a bevel, how deep an opening inset, and how much per-instance variation.
objective: A close-up capture of the hero at 3 m shows at least two features from each of the silhouette, medium and fine bands, and two instances of the same blueprint are visibly different.
intent_signals: how much detail should a building have
example_prompts: My village buildings look like grey boxes when I zoom in.
How much geometric detail should the hero prop carry?
not_for: Polygon budgets for a specific target device.
Any claim about how real buildings, tools or creatures are constructed.

principles: Detail is a ladder, not a quantity. An object that fails at one rung cannot be rescued by more of another: a thousand rivets do not fix a silhouette that reads as a box.
The silhouette is what survives fog, distance and backlight. Author it before any surface treatment exists.
Thickness is the medium band's whole job. An opening cut flush with a wall is a decal at every distance; an opening set back reads as built even at low resolution.
The fine band is what a viewer discovers, not what they are shown. Its features exist to reward a close-up, so they only need to survive at the close-up distance.
implementation: Silhouette: two to four profile events per object — a roof pitch change, an overhang, a chimney, a mast. Check by rendering the object as a flat black shape against the sky and asking whether it is still identifiable.
Medium: 3 to 6 features per square metre of visible wall or shell. Openings inset 10-15 cm behind the surrounding surface for a building, 2-4 cm for a hand prop.
Fine: bevel every hard edge that catches a highlight, 2-4 cm at building scale and 2-5 mm at prop scale. Nothing that a viewer must be closer than 1 m to see.

Per-instance variation: 3-8 percent hue offset, 5-12 percent uniform scale, and full yaw rotation on any object placed more than three times. Below 3 percent the copies read as clones; above 12 percent they read as different objects.
Spend the budget top down. If the poly budget forces a cut, cut the fine band first and the silhouette last.
observable_checks: Capture the hero at 3 m and count features per band; two or more from each band passes.
Render the hero silhouette as a flat black shape: a viewer who knows the subject still names it.
Place two instances of the same blueprint side by side with different seeds: hue and scale differences are visible without measuring.
Probe one opening: the inset depth measured in the scene is inside the stated range for its scale.

defaults.rationale: Tuned on the village kit blueprints at 1280x720, ACESFilmic tone mapping and exposure 1.0, viewed at a 3 m close-up. The bands are what separated a readable kit building from a flat box in those captures.

known_limits: Authored creative starting values. Nothing here measures any real object, and no perceptual study supports the ranges.
Tuned at 1280x720 with ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0 and no post-processing; a bloom-heavy or low-resolution target changes which band survives.
The per-square-metre numbers assume a village-scale diorama. A vehicle interior or a molecular model needs its own ladder.
creative_affordances: Deliberately strip the fine band for a flat-shaded or papercraft look and say so; the ladder then has two rungs by choice, not by omission.
Push the variation percentages far past the stated band for a deliberately chaotic settlement.
